transcript.text: Our Bosch dryer keeps stopping with the empty water container light on but the container is empty?? We've emptied it like 5 times

This usually happens because the appliance thinks the tank is full when it isn't, often due to poor contact or a stuck sensor rather than actual water being present. Please slide the container out, check it's clean and undamaged, then push it back in firmly until it clicks into place. If the light stays on after doing this carefully, we need to check if the internal float switch is sticking.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]
Yes I've pushed it back in firmly, it clicks, but the light still comes on. There's a slimy bit on the container filter which I cleaned. Still stops 20-40 mins in though.

[Heading: Stuck float switch or blocked sump]
Please unplug the dryer first for safety. Locate the sump area at the bottom front (often behind a small flap or near the filter housing) and find the small white plastic float/lever inside it. Gently push it up and down to check if it moves freely. If it is stiff, stuck, or doesn't spring back, that is likely the cause. If it moves perfectly freely but the light stays on, the switch itself may be faulty or there is a blockage in the pump inlet.

I found a small cover at the bottom front and behind it was grey slimy water and fluff, so I wiped out what I could reach. Ran it again and it went about 60 mins this time but the light came on again. I couldn't see a white lever or float, to be honest, and I can't pull the dryer out as it's stacked on the washer.

[Heading: Condensate pump or sump blockage]
The fact that it ran for 60 minutes after you cleaned the sump suggests the blockage was temporary but the underlying issue remains. Since you couldn't see a float lever and there was slimy water at the bottom, the condensate pump (which lifts water from the sump to the container) is likely either blocked by that sludge or has failed mechanically. To confirm this safely: please plug the dryer back in and start a programme. Listen closely at the bottom front flap area for about 5–10 minutes. Do you hear the pump humming or buzzing? If it hums but no water moves, the pump is blocked or jammed. If there is silence and the drum gets warm, the pump motor may have failed. Please let me know what sound (if any) you hear.
Honestly I don't know what I'm supposed to be listening for, so I can't tell you if the pump is running. I can't get round the back either with it stacked. What should I be listening for exactly?

[Heading: Blocked condensate pump or sump blockage]
I understand that listening for a specific hum can be tricky. Since we know there was slimy sludge in the sump earlier, the pump is likely blocked by that debris or has failed to move it. Please start a drying programme and leave it running for about 10 minutes. Then, carefully open the door and put your hand inside (don't touch any metal parts directly if you are unsure). If the drum feels warm or hot, the heater is working but the water isn't being pumped away, confirming the pump is blocked or stuck. If the drum remains cold, the issue might be electrical (the pump isn't getting power) or a sensor fault. Let me know if it gets hot or stays cold.

I can do that, but it's not really answering my question about what the pump sounds like. Can I just try it? Does the drum being warm actually tell us anything when it already heats and dries partially?

[Heading: Blocked condensate pump or sump due to sludge/fluff]
I understand your frustration; checking drum temperature can feel irrelevant when you know it’s heating up. The reason I asked was to distinguish between a pump that is trying to work (and failing because of sludge) versus one that has completely failed electrically or mechanically. Given the slimy water we found earlier and the fact that it ran for 60 minutes before stopping again, the most likely cause is that the condensate pump is blocked by that same sludge. Since you can't move the appliance or hear the pump clearly, let's try a direct test for blockage. Look at the bottom rear or front of the dryer; many Bosch models have a small emergency drain hose with a clip. Place a shallow tray under it, open the clip, and see if water flows out freely (indicating the sump is full but the pump can't move it) or if nothing comes out (suggesting the sensor is faulty or the pump is completely dead). If you don't see a drain hose, we may need to consider that the internal float switch is sticking due to the sludge residue.

No, there's no drain hose fitted as far as I know, and I can't see one at the front. I can't get round the back with it stacked on the washer. Is there anything else I can check from the front, or is this a job for an engineer?

[Heading: Blocked or failed condensate pump]
Given that you cannot access the rear to check for a drain hose, and we have already found slimy sludge in the sump area, this points strongly to the internal condensate pump being blocked by debris or having failed mechanically. I recommend calling an engineer to replace the condensate pump assembly. They will have the tools to clear any remaining sludge from the internal pipes as well, ensuring it doesn't happen again immediately.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
